body:
`cps/static/js/reading/annotations.js`:

    function safeColorToken(color) {
        var c = (color == null ? "" : String(color)).trim().toLowerCase()
                  .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "");
        return c || "unknown";
    }

It derives a semantic colour name by DELETING characters, so a token this app
cannot name can reduce to one it can. MEASURED in the browser against a
container running #1737, 2026-08-18:

    "yellow!"  -> "yellow"      <- invents a palette colour
    "#123456"  -> "123456"      <- raw hex reaches a CSS class name
    "olive"    -> "olive"       (harmless, no rule exists)
    null       -> "unknown"     (correct)

Two consequences, both in the legacy EPUB reader only:

1. the sidebar row gets `cwa-annotation-yellow` and the edit popup shows the
   yellow swatch as the selected one, for a highlight whose stored colour is
   not yellow and is not known;
2. `cwa-annotation-123456` is emitted as a class for an unrecognised hex.

This VIOLATES the invariant #1737 established and that
`cps/services/annotation_colors.py` states in its own docstring — a consumer
that keys a palette must use `to_known_display_name`, which answers None
rather than a token no palette has an entry for. The overlay FILL is not
affected: `colorToRgba` resolves the same tokens independently and correctly
paints the neutral, so nothing on the page is painted a wrong colour. The
defect is confined to the class name and the popup's pressed state.

REACHABILITY IS LOW and that is why this is filed rather than fixed in #1737.
Only a preserved unknown token reaches `safeColorToken` at all — every colour
the server can name arrives as a name. Getting a punctuation-bearing token
into the column needs a third-party client to push one through
`apply_portable` (KOReader's own palette names — olive, cyan, purple — all
pass through harmlessly; none of them reduces to a palette word).

PRE-EXISTING, and #1737 improved it: the same function used to return the
literal "yellow" for an absent colour, which was the invented-colour bug for
EVERY note-only row rather than for a contrived token.

FIX: validate against the known display vocabulary instead of sanitising.
Ship the list of known names to the client (or inline it beside NAMED_RGB) and
return "unknown" for anything not in it; keep a separate helper for the
four-colour editable palette so the popup's pressed state and the CSS class
cannot disagree. A behavioural test should drive the popup for a grey row and
assert no swatch is pressed.

Found by an adversarial Sol review of the final #1737 diff and confirmed in a
browser; not caused by that branch.
title: The legacy reader's safeColorToken can strip an unknown colour down to a palette name
